top.line: Maya Dotan's seven identity layers for AI agents, and how our agent teams answer each one.
top.para: A name, a key per session, a For: line, a behaviour policy, decisions as pages, and a signed record.

in-short.line: Her map, naming, keys, authority as policy, reputation as a record.

map.line: 190 projects from 81 organisations; authority has the most work, naming and reputation the least.
map.para: She asked for missing projects; ours answers every row.

naming.line: A dotted address says what the agent is, which team, and for whom: place.olhao@PrompTugal.dinis.
naming.para: The cheapest layer with the biggest return.

keys.line: Each session makes a P-256 key; 147 entries in the registry, 98 active, 49 superseded.
keys.para: Identity is name, current key and policy together.

principal.line: The name ends with the person, and every commit says For: whom; only the person instructs.
principal.para: Other people's agents work under an external policy.

authority.line: An Agent Behaviour Policy per role, 45 roles in one file, kept by hooks on every tool call.
authority.para: Some limits sit above the agents; the rest were observed, with a circuit breaker.

approval.line: Decisions are pages, asks wait in a status file, irreversible acts stay drafts, only the person merges.
approval.para: Approval at altitude, not per action.

reputation.line: Reputation as a signed record: 2,032 run reports, hourly reports, reviews and daily debriefs.
reputation.para: Trust becomes a question you can answer from evidence.

adds.line: Plain keys and files suffice; naming and reputation are by-products; enforcement is the hard part.

limits.line: Inside teams we run; mostly observed, not blocked; session keys by design; her counts are hers.

sources.line: Maya Dotan's post, the PrompTugal.news repository files, abp.sgit.ai and earlier articles.
